w: Liseberg has pulled about three million visitors a year since 1923, and its wooden coaster Balder was twice voted the best wooden track on Earth. Come autumn the park swaps thrill rides for houses of horror, then a Christmas market serving mulled wine and reindeer-meat doner kebab.
s: A wooden coaster, then a reindeer kebab Christmas.
_facts: Amusement park opened in 1923, second most visited theme park in Scandinavia with around three million visitors annually
Wooden roller coaster Balder voted Best Wooden Tracked Roller Coaster in the world in 2003 and 2005
Open October to December with a Halloween season and a Christmas market serving mulled wine and reindeer-meat doner kebab

w: Serneke topped this Lindholmen tower out in 2023 at 246 metres and 74 floors - tall enough to overtake Malmo's Turning Torso as the tallest building in the Nordic countries the moment it passed 193 metres. Residents started moving in before the building itself was even finished.
s: The Nordics' tallest tower, occupied mid-build.
_facts: Mixed-use skyscraper in Lindholmen, built by Serneke, started 2019, topped out June 2023, 246 metres tall, 74 floors, completed autumn 2024
Tallest building in Sweden, Scandinavia and the Nordic countries; surpassed Malmo's Turning Torso on 22 September 2022 at 193 metres
First inhabitants started moving in from August 2023

w: Haga started out as a rough working-class suburb that locals avoided; a 1980s renovation saved its wooden houses - some genuine, some replicas - and made it Gothenburg's cafe district. Its population has dropped by more than two-thirds since 1900, and, oddly, it's the smallest parish in Sweden.
s: A rough suburb reborn as Gothenburg's cafe quarter.
_facts: City district renowned for picturesque wooden houses, 19th-century atmosphere and cafes; originally a working-class suburb with a bad reputation
Major renovation in the 1980s: houses renovated or torn down and replaced by post-modernist replicas
Population about 4,000 in 2006 versus 15,000 a century earlier; also a parish, areawise the smallest parish in Sweden

w: One of the more expansive botanical gardens anywhere in Europe, this sprawling collection gives Gothenburg a proper green lung within easy reach of the city centre - a quiet counterweight to the amusement park and museums clustered nearby.
s: One of Europe's more expansive botanical gardens.
_facts: One of the larger botanical gardens in Europe, located in Gothenburg

w: Built from the wound-down collections of Gothenburg's old ethnographic museum, this 2004 arrival opened with an exhibition on AIDS in the age of globalization rather than a safe survey of artifacts - a statement of intent it's kept up since, sitting right beside Liseberg and the Universeum science centre.
s: Opened with an exhibition on AIDS, not artifacts.
_facts: Opened 2004, builds on the collections of the former Goteborgs Etnografiska Museum that closed in 2000
Opening exhibitions included 'No Name Fever: AIDS in the age of globalization'
Situated next to the Universeum science centre and the Liseberg amusement park, close to Korsvagen

w: Down at Lilla Bommen on the waterfront, Gothenburg's opera house runs its own resident dance company alongside the opera itself, led in recent years by Katrin Hall under artistic director Henning Ruhe.
s: Opera and dance, side by side at Lilla Bommen.
_facts: Opera house at Lilla Bommen in Gothenburg
Artistic Director for opera Henning Ruhe since 2019; Katrin Hall leads the Gothenburg Opera Dance Company

w: Olof Palme cut the ribbon on this bridge in 1966; its clearance sits below cruise-ship standard, so the largest ships dock outside rather than pass beneath. In 1993 the city spent 36,000 litres of paint turning it green for the World Athletics Championships, later serving twice as the Volvo Ocean Race finish line.
s: Painted green for a championship, too low for cruise ships.
_facts: Suspension bridge over the Gota alv connecting Hisingen to the mainland, inaugurated 8 November 1966 by minister Olof Palme
Clearance below deck 45 metres, below the international standard of 65 metres for the largest cruise ships, so many dock outside the bridge
Painted green using about 36,000 litres of paint for the 1995 World Championships in Athletics
Finish line for the 2005-06 and 2014-15 Volvo Ocean Race

w: Sweden built this sea fort in 1653 to guard its one and only outlet to the open Atlantic - and then watched it sit largely untested for two centuries, seeing real combat just once, during the Great Northern War, before finally standing down in 1869.
s: Guarding Sweden's only Atlantic door since 1653.
_facts: Sea fort on the island of Kyrkogardsholmen, protected what was then Sweden's only access to the North Sea and Atlantic Ocean
Construction began 1653, remained in service until 1869
Saw significant action only once, in the Great Northern War

w: World of Volvo opened in April 2024, just months after the old Volvo Museum shut its doors for good, taking over as the jointly owned showcase for a car brand that's practically a national institution in its home city.
s: A car brand's heritage, freshly rehoused in 2024.
_facts: Automotive museum and experience centre, opened April 2024, jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Volvo Group
Opened after the former Volvo Museum closed in December 2023

w: This medieval settlement once anchored southern Bohuslan, its ruins marking the former fortification at Ragnhildsholmen - a scrap of the Norse-era world that predates modern Gothenburg entirely.
s: A Norse-era settlement older than the city itself.
_facts: Medieval settlement in southern Bohuslan, in what is now Kungalv Municipality
Site of the former fortification at Ragnhildsholmen

w: Gothenburg built this hilltop redoubt and its twin, Skansen Lejonet, as a matched pair of defenses against a Danish attack that - like so much military architecture of the era - never actually came. It watches over the Haga district from Risasberget hill, built the same era as the sea fort at New Alvsborg.
s: A hilltop fort built against a Danish attack.
_facts: Redoubt on the hill Risasberget, in the Haga district
Built together with its twin Skansen Lejonet to protect Gothenburg against possible Danish attack
Similar purpose to the sea fort of New Alvsborg, built around the same time

w: August Kruger raised this Romanesque Revival synagogue in 1855, seating 300 worshippers near Drottningtorget - one of Sweden's older surviving synagogues, and listed as a protected building since 1999.
_facts: Conservative Jewish congregation and synagogue at Ostra Larmgatan 12, near Drottningtorget
Designed by August Kruger in Romanesque Revival style, completed 1855, 300 seats
Classified as a listed building in 1999

w: This city museum runs its history collection out of the actual East India House, built in 1762 as the Swedish East India Company's own offices - so its permanent exhibition on the company sits inside the very building it once worked from. The wider collection spans the Viking Age to the present.
s: Trading-company history inside the company's own house.
_facts: Local history museum located in the East India House, originally built as Swedish East India Company offices in 1762
City museum established 1861, displays Gothenburg and West Sweden's history from the Viking Age to the present
Permanent exhibition about the Swedish East India Company

w: Sigfrid Ericson planted this National Romantic church on Masthugget hill in 1914 with a tower rising 60 metres above the Gota alv - tall enough, and striking enough, that it's become one of the handful of buildings that reads as Gothenburg's skyline itself.
s: A 60-metre tower that reads as the skyline itself.
_facts: Built in 1914 on a high hill (Masthugget) close to the Gota alv, tower 60 metres high
National Romantic style, designed by Sigfrid Ericson
Become one of the symbols of Gothenburg, a popular tourist attraction

w: The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community completed this hilltop mosque in 1976, and it's widely reckoned the first purpose-built mosque in the whole of Sweden - one of the earliest permanent Islamic places of worship anywhere in Scandinavia. It still holds 400 worshippers on its original 7,000-square-metre site.
_facts: Established 1975, completed 1976, built by the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community
Widely regarded as the first purpose-built mosque in Sweden and one of the earliest permanent Islamic places of worship in Scandinavia
Site of approximately 7,000 square metres, capacity of 400 worshippers

w: King Carl XVI Gustaf inaugurated this vertical-lift bridge in 2021 after four years of construction, replacing the old Gotaalvbro as the main link between Hisingen island and the Gothenburg mainland.
s: A vertical-lift bridge opened by the king in 2021.
_facts: Vertical-lift bridge in central Gothenburg connecting Hisingen island to the mainland
Constructed 2017-2021, replacing the Gotaalvbro
Inaugurated 5 September 2021 by King Carl XVI Gustaf
